speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in to report weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm. To help me determine the cause, have you noticed if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually? Do you have any history of neck pain, recent trauma, or high blood pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor).

I have noted the significant "red flags" you mentioned, including unexplained weight loss, diabetes, and your bodybuilding history. Given the progressive weakness, sensory loss, and systemic symptoms, I need to visualize the apex of your right lung immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray (Right Apex) AND Chest_CT with contrast.
